items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: You were, according to Gene Lees, I believe said you were the biggest Bill Evans nut he ever knew.

ctx.x: You were, according to Gene Lees, I believe said you were the biggest Bill Evans nut he ever knew.

Probably. Probably. I heard Bill Evans, this I guess is a story that’s been told often but it’s worth telling again. I first heard Bill Evans under the most wrong circumstances imaginable. One of the first artists that Riverside got involved with was Mundell Lowe, and Mundell — who is still alive and well and an excellent guitarist — but was very much a part of a very white jazz scene of that time. But he had known Bill back at — what is it, northeast or southeast or whatever Louisiana College, the small…
